BLOCKER: CL-006 not satisfied: the Gate-1 context embeds no Gate 1.5 findings/dispositions, so approval is invalid while any BLOCKER/MAJOR is PENDING (enforced by `gate1_check.py`).
Cross-tenant RLS test isn't specified to run as a non-superuser/non-BYPASSRLS role; as written it could pass vacuously under the same privileged connection used to seed data.
MAJOR: Dual conflict-target ambiguity: `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` (PK on id) coexists with retry on `uq_artifacts_name_revision`; a re-ingest of a previously-seen payload collides on id, so the computed "next revision" never lands — the returned revision can diverge from the stored row. State the id/revision invariant and add a test (revert-to-old-payload case).

`--verify` exit semantics incomplete: AC only covers drift; design doesn't state that `failed` (unreadable source, missing object row, Head error) also exits non-zero — an unreachable/corrupt store could report failure yet exit 0.

Observability gap (checklist 10): no metrics or structured logs defined (ingest duration, drift count, verify failures, orphan writes); `run_id` exists only in stdout report, so scheduled-run failures are undiagnosable.
`needs_api` decision (checklist 8) is never stated; explicitly record "no API surface, operator CLI only" with rationale in the Gate 1 doc.
`--allow-bypassrls` is a runtime RLS escape hatch; require it to be denied in test/CI paths and emit a high-severity audit log on use, otherwise the tenant-isolation guarantee is advisory.
MINOR: AC says "content-addressed key" but keys are tenant-prefixed — wording conflict, and cross-tenant identical content is stored twice; document the trade-off.
Orphaned objects (object written, metadata failed) rely on a future objreconcile with no retention/reconcile trigger defined in this design — unbounded garbage risk.
`pfingest --verify` streaming fallback reads the full object with no stated byte cap; the 256MiB ingest cap doesn't clearly apply.
`scripts/dev/gate0_check.py` fix is listed in `in_scope` despite "separate commit" — enforce the split so the registry flip stays independently revertable.
No registry/doc record of which of the 11 targets are multi-file (e.g. `intake-files`) vs single-file — command template per target should be pinned to avoid operator variance.
NIT: Add a golden-file test for the pinned `pf.intake-ingest/1` JSON (field names, enum values, UUIDv4 `run_id` format) to prevent silent schema drift.
Report is stdout + optional `--report-file`; consider failing closed if `--report-file` path is unwritable for scheduled runs.
SUMMARY: Sound approach: Go ingestion over existing ports, content-addressed immutability, idempotent upserts, honest `backfill_status=pending`, and Gate-1.5 hardening cover most guardrails.

Top risks: dual conflict-target/revision invariant is under-specified and untested for the revert case; RLS test validity and `--allow-bypassrls` weaken the isolation claim; observability and `needs_api` checklist items are unanswered.
Verdict: proceed only after CL-006 dispositions are embedded and the MAJOR items are dispositioned; no schema change means rollback risk remains low.
